name: Radio Sutatenza rural radio schools
description: An educational radio-school system combining broadcasts with community support for rural learners in Colombia.

impact.note: Broadcast schooling brought literacy to rural Colombians who had no school access; one region, with radio-school successors in other countries.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: José Joaquín Salcedo began a rural radio-school project from the parish of Sutatenza, Boyacá, Colombia.
events.place_note: Early broadcasts reached households in the rural locality of Irzón.

evidence.supports: The nomination dates the start of the project to 1947 and names Salcedo and the parish of Sutatenza, Boyacá.
Places assembly of the first transmitter in Sutatenza in 1947 and describes early reception by households in Irzón.
Places the present-day municipal seat used as the approximate map point.

events.caveats: This dates the local start of the project. Irzón was an early receiving locality. Accounts differ about the day of the first cultural broadcast.

evidence.supports: Nomination dates start of rural radio-school project to 1947 and identifies Salcedo.

date.label: 7 November 1954
date.basis: Date of the ceremony given by the film and speech catalogue descriptions.

events.statement: A high-power transmitter and new broadcasting equipment for the radio schools were inaugurated in Sutatenza, with President Gustavo Rojas Pinilla in attendance.

evidence.locator: Collection description, first paragraph; Ficha técnica
evidence.supports: Dates and locates the inauguration and identifies its broadcasting equipment and presidential attendance.

evidence.locator: Introductory numbered point 3, CD8409 / CD8136 title
evidence.supports: Dates Rojas Pinilla’s inauguration speech in Sutatenza to 7 November 1954.

events.caveats: The sources identify an equipment inauguration. The transmitter model, rated power, and additional audience reached remain uncertain.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: UNESCO reported that the educational project reached 687 Colombian localities and trained 20,039 rural leaders.

evidence.supports: UNESCO reports coverage of 687 localities and 20,039 trained rural leaders over the project.

events.caveats: Retrospective cumulative figures across the educational project; no single-year listener count or inferred contemporaneous reach.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in cited evidence for this scope, not a global priority claim.

unresolved.note: The ACPO chronology used by Bernal gives 28 September 1947 for the first cultural broadcast. The Banco de la República bulletin gives 16 November. A dated station log, script, or transmission recording could distinguish the early trials and locate the transmitting room.

evidence.supports: Dates the first cultural broadcast to 28 September 1947 and identifies the underlying ACPO chronology.

measures.subject: Radio Sutatenza educational project
measures.conditions: UNESCO retrospective figure across the program; not a count of listeners.

evidence.supports: UNESCO reports coverage of 687 localities and 20,039 trained rural leaders over the project.
